It's not a big deal. Just start DCAing now, when you have extra cash bi-weekly or monthly. If you already have like $50k cash or something, just DCA it once a week over a 12-month period, into 2 or 3 different funds.

It's not significant enough to matter.

The "statistics" assume both investments are being deployed on January 1st of each year. But, that's not how anyone actually invests. Nobody holds like $10k in cash the previous year and then decides on January 1st of the next year to start DCAing or putting it all in at once. And if they do (like an IRA), people will clear the DCA over a few months, not the entire year.

A more realistic scenario is something like this:
- Person A has a biweekly contribution of $500 into an index fund. He starts doing this January 1st. Person A never saves up $6k in cash to lump-sum invest in the first place.
- Person B chooses to save up the extra $500 in cash he earns biweekly in a savings account or money market fund. On June 1st, Person B puts the entire $6k lump-sum of cash into an index fund. He then saves up again to put another lump-sum of $6k in on December 1st.

In this scenario, Person A will most likely outperform Person B, because half of his yearly contributions are already compounding before Person B puts in his lump-sum on June 1st.

If you don't have any massive cash holdings (excluding your emergency cash), then DCAing and lump-sum are literally the same thing. You're putting in a "lump-sum" of $500 every two weeks.
